articles.title: Deere Jumps as Tractor Maker Sees Upturn in Farm Economy
articles.mainIdea: Deere Jumps as Tractor Maker Sees Upturn in Farm Economy
articles.summary: Bloomberg: Deere Jumps as Tractor Maker Sees Upturn in Farm Economy. “While the global large agriculture industry continues to experience challenges, we’re encouraged by the ongoing recovery in demand within both the construction and small agriculture segments,” Chief Executive Officer John May said in the company earnings statement Thursday. First quarter adjusted earnings of $2.42 a share, while down from a year earlier, handily beat the average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg of $2.05 a share. The results were “driven by better-than expected sales and margins across all units on higher shipments as order books strengthened,” Bloomberg Intelligence analysts wrote in a report.

articles.title: Deere Stock Surges On Earnings As Ag Cycle Bottoms
articles.mainIdea: Deere Stock Surges On Earnings As Ag Cycle Bottoms
articles.summary: Investor's Business Daily: Deere Stock Surges On Earnings As Ag Cycle Bottoms. Deere earnings mowed down estimates for the fiscal first quarter, though still fell sharply from a year ago as the company boosted its 2026 outlook despite predicting another down year for sales of big agricultural machinery. "While the global large agriculture industry continues to experience challenges, we're encouraged by the ongoing recovery in demand within both the construction and small agriculture segments," CEO John May said in the earnings statement. Results: Deere posted Q1 earnings per share of $2.42, down 24% from a year ago but 32 cents ahead of forecasts.
